full_judgment:
3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit filing a written statement denying the allegation contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable, that it is barred by limitation, that the plaintiff proposed to sell the land in question and defendant No. 1 agreed to purchase the same at the highest market price and that the plaintiff went to Bheramara Sub-Registrar's Office on her own will and that after receiving the consideration money she executed and registered the kabala. The suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The trial Court decreed the suit on the findings, inter alia, that the suit is not barred by limitation as the plaintiff herself proved her date of knowledge as on 19-2-77 and as the suit was filed on 7-3-77; that the plaintiff being a pardahanshin village woman did not get independent and free advice before executing the kabala and found that the impugned kabala is collusive, fraudulent, without any consideration and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 6. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in revision set aside the finding of the lower appellate Court on the question of limitation and also found that the kabala was obtained fraudulently by the son defendant No. 2 and his wife defendant No. 1 taking the plaintiff to Bheramara and that the plaintiff being an illiterate pardanashin village woman did not get independent and disinterested advice in the matter of executing and registering the kabala. Consequently he decreed the suit. 

 7. Leave was granted only to consider the question of limitation as to whether the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division correctly decided the question of limitation on proper consideration of the evidence on record in view of  the statement made in the plaint showing the date of knowledge to be on 19-2-77 and in view of the fact that the suit was filed on 7-3-77 and in further view of the deposition of the  plaintiff that she disclosed to her another son Keamuddin on the day of registration of the impugned kabala, namely, 17-10-66, that defendant No.2 had cheated her and registered the kabala. 

 8. The material question as per the leave order is, whether the question of limitation was correctly decided by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division. 

 9. PW 1 Majerunnessa, plaintiff, herself deposed before the trial Court that for the first time she came to know about the impugned kabala on 19-2-77 and she filed the suit within time from the date of her knowledge. She further stated that the suit was filed on 7-3-77. The defendant appellants in their written statement raised objection contending that the suit was barred by limitation. But during the trial defendant did not adduce any evidence to show as to how the suit was barred by limitation. According to the testimony of PW 1 she has been possessing the suit land even after the disputed kabala. It is in evidence that the plaintiff and her son defendant No. 2 were looking after the property. She being an illiterate pardanashin lady relied upon her son and had no knowledge about the fraudulent deed regarding the property. She never suspected that any fraudulent deed was obtained by her son defendant No.2 nor she had any knowledge as to in whose name the record of right has been published. At the time when the record of right was going to be prepared in that area she came to know for the first time that the land had been recorded in the name of her son's wife defendant No.1. After having definite knowledge on 19-2-77 she filed the suit after taking necessary instructions and advice on 7-3-77. The learned Single Judge correctly found that the lower appellate Court relied upon some minor discrepancies in the evidence of PW 1 and wrongly held that the suit was barred by limitation 

 10. As a matter of fact in the plaint nowhere the plaintiff stated that she disclosed to her son Keamuddin on 17-10-66 about the registration of the kabala. There is no averment that on 17-10-66 the plaintiff suspected about the registration of the kabala and that she had definite knowledge on that day. In the deposition of the plaintiff there is no categorical assertion that she disclosed about the date of knowledge to her said son on 17-10-66. In the plaint it has been stated that after obtaining the certified copy of the kabala the plaintiff had definite know ledge on 19-2-77 in respect of the fraudulent and collusive kabala. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division correctly evaluated the evidence of PW 1 Majirunnessa and held that it is not correct to hold that PW 1 knew about the sale in the year 1966. As the deed was executed and registered by a village illiterate pardanashin lady onus lies heavily upon the defendant's son and daughter-in-law to show that the deed was legally executed and registered with the free will and consent of the plaintiff having free and independent advice. Hence, the learned Single Judge was right in .holding that the defendants totally failed to prove that the suit was barred by limitation. In the present case fraud having been perpetuated on the mother, the question of limitation will run from the date of knowledge and consequently the suit cannot be barred by limitation. In that view of the matter the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division rightly set aside the finding of the lower appellate Court on the question of limitation and decreed the suit.
